deadline.value: To be considered for any Imperial scholarship, including department scholarships and President's PhD Scholarships, apply by Round 1 (1 Nov 2026), Round 2 (11 Jan 2027) or Round 3 (1 Mar 2027, if scholarships remain). Most Chemical Engineering scholarships are allocated in Round 1, with interviews in late November or early December.
deadline.quote: You will need to submit your PhD application by the following deadlines in order to be considered for any Imperial scholarships: | Round 1: 1 November 2026 | Round 2: 11 January 2027 | Round 3: 1 March 2027 | Please note that the majority of Chemical Engineering PhD Scholarships are likely to be allocated in Round 1.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for this field; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Scholarship applicants do not need a supervisor first: a selection panel shortlists and interviews them, then allocates projects. Self-funded or externally sponsored applicants must find a supervisor who will put them forward for interview.
supervisor.quote: An academic selection panel will screen the applications that demonstrate the necessary achievement and potential and will shortlist the most outstanding candidates for interview. | you will need to identify a potential supervisor (the list of academic research groups may be useful) who is prepared to supervise you subject to successful interview with an independent academic panel.

funding.value: Applicants are considered automatically for Chemical Engineering PhD Scholarships and other college-administered scholarships, which are very competitive. EPSRC DTP places go only to candidates who meet EPSRC eligibility. Strong applicants who miss out may be passed to supervisors with funded projects.
funding.quote: you will automatically be considered for the Chemical Engineering PhD Scholarships and any other College-administered scholarships for which you may be eligible.

also.quote: The scholarships are very competitive and our aim is to select the most outstanding PhD students and offer them financial support.

entry_route.value: Applicants are expected to hold a First Class (Distinction) master's or equivalent in engineering, design or science. A 2:1 (Merit) master's may be considered only with extensive research or industry experience.
entry_route.quote: Applicants are expected to have a First Class (Distinction) Degree or equivalent at Masters level in a relevant engineering, design or scientific discipline. | In exceptional cases where extensive research/industry experience can be demonstrated, candidates with a UK-equivalent of 2:1 (Merit) at

toefl_min.value: Chemical Engineering requires Imperial's Higher English level: TOEFL iBT 100 overall (min 22 in each section), or 5.0 on the new scale.
toefl_min.quote: You must meet the College’s English language requirement at the higher level.

ielts_min.value: Chemical Engineering requires Imperial's Higher English level: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall (min 6.5 in each element).
ielts_min.quote: You must meet the College’s English language requirement at the higher level.

notes: Apply to 'Chemical Engineering (PhD)'. The department has about 220 PhD students. Scholarship interviews last 20 minutes (Teams if you are outside London). The master's-level entry rule comes from Imperial's draft PhD course page (dev-sites, marked 'Entry in 2023'); the live department pages give no grade.
